meta.what: Economic value to Ukraine of every loan, loan guarantee and swap line in the Kiel Ukraine Support Tracker (Release 31, allocations to 31 Aug 2026), by lender and year, plus new multilateral lending (IMF, World Bank, EBRD, CEB) not already credited to donors, credited to members by shareholding.
meta.units: EUR bn, nominal; 2026 = January-August, not annualised. USD converted with ECB yearly averages 2022 1.053, 2023 1.081, 2024 1.082, 2025 1.13, 2026 1.16.
meta.method: Economic value = face value x grant element; grant element = 1 - present value of Ukraine's repayments (interest + principal) per euro lent, discounted at the rate Ukraine would otherwise pay for long-term money. Discount rate per disbursement year: low = OECD DAC ODA rates (7% for 2022-23 when Ukraine was lower-middle income, 6% from 2024) ~ Ukraine's 2021 Eurobond yields (6.3-6.9%); central = 10% (IMF/OECD classic convention, bottom of post-restructuring Eurobond yields 10-16%); high = 15% (2022-23), 14% (2024), 13% (2025-26) ~ post-restructuring yields. Wartime spot yields of 30-60%+ are not used: they price a haircut on old bonds, not a 35-year cost of funds. EU interest subsidies: paid by EU budget/member states to end-2027 (legal), then low = Ukraine pays EU funding cost from 2028, central = subsidy continues to 2034 (next MFF), high = for the loan's life. Guarantees on IBRD sovereign loans are valued at the grant element of the IBRD loan they enable (the loan would not exist without them); other guarantees at 10/25/40% of face (expected loss covered plus cheaper credit). ERA loans (repaid from Russian assets) are left out, as in the map.

meta.how_to_use: For each country replace the face value of loans/guarantees in the net shift (Kiel loans + guarantees + swap, EU share included) by loans_guarantees_economic_value: the change is net_adjustment_vs_face. In the cost view, the grant element here can replace LOAN_GRANT_ELEMENT (0.3). multilateral_new is a new, separate part toward Ukraine.

eu_institutions.note: Kiel EU_INST incl. EIB. Includes the Ukraine Support Loan 2026 (3.2 macro-financial + 8.37 military window, the latter in Kiel's military category, not in loans_face_value), split over the 24 guarantor members only. Guarantees: Ukraine Investment Framework guarantees to EIB/EBRD/IFC etc.

prewar_baseline.note: Pre-war official lending to Ukraine (2019-2021 average): EU MFA ~EUR 0.4bn/yr (COVID-MFA tranches Dec 2020 and Oct 2021), IMF USD 0.93bn/yr, IBRD USD 0.75bn/yr, EBRD EUR 1.1bn/yr. The map has no pre-war baseline for aid; the IMF/IBRD/EBRD baselines are already subtracted in multilateral_new. If the builder wants a baseline for EU loans: EUR 0.4bn x grant element 0.40 (15-year MFA at EU cost, 7% discount) = EUR 0.16bn/yr EU-wide, split by EU budget share.

possible_gaps_not_added: World Bank lists a Canadian guarantee of USD 841m to PEACE (IBRD); Kiel records only a EUR 36.5m Canadian EBRD guarantee. If confirmed and missing from Kiel, its value would be ~EUR 0.8bn x 0.13/0.41/0.58.

IDS shows IDA disbursements to Ukraine of USD 4.8bn in 2024 that are not explained by IDA's own lending (probably donor money routed through IDA-administered instruments); not credited to IDA donors here.
Israel's 2023 USD 200m loan-guarantee offer (aid_gaps-notes.md) is not in Kiel and not added.

overlaps: 1) Kiel aid (kiel.json): this file does not add aid; it re-values loans/guarantees that are already in Kiel's financial (and, for the Ukraine Support Loan and some guarantees, military) allocations at face value. Use net_adjustment_vs_face, never add economic value on top of the face value. 2) ERA loans (US 18.3, EU 18.1, Canada 3.26, UK 2.65, Japan 1.58) are excluded here as in the map (era_excluded_face only as a check). 3) EU-level split: eu_level_share uses Kiel's EU budget shares, with the 2026 Ukraine Support Loan over the 24 guarantors only, i.e. the same correction as apply_audit(); do not apply that correction twice. 4) Multilateral: World Bank lending backed by donor guarantees (Japan ADVANCE, UK, Netherlands, Sweden, Denmark, Lithuania, Spain) and donor trust funds (PEACE grants: US 26bn; URTF; FREE; F.O.R.T.I.S. = US ERA money) is in Kiel under the donor and is NOT credited again to World Bank shareholders; IBRD own-risk lending did not rise above its pre-war level. EIB lending is in Kiel's EU_INST (split by budget share) and is not credited again. EBRD and CEB volumes are reduced by the donor-backed share (EBRD EUR 3.4bn donor resources of 9.1bn; CEB about half EU/Italian-guaranteed). IMF: the Administered Account loans (Canada, Netherlands) are bilateral loans in Kiel and are not IMF purchases. 5) Switzerland's EUR 0.10bn EBRD capital-increase guarantee is in Kiel; its EBRD share here is small (~0.01bn) and a different thing (EBRD's own lending), so both are kept. 6) Flowback: Spain's 2026 instruments, UK Export Finance (Urenco) and Swedish/French export-credit guarantees support the donor's own exporters; flowback.json does not cover them (it is military-aid based), so no double count, but the builder may want to note it.
notes: Totals 2022-2026 (EUR bn, face -> economic value low/central/high): EU institutions 72.7 -> 35.3/54.0/63.2; Japan 10.2 -> 2.0/4.4/6.0; Canada 5.1 -> 1.5/2.2/2.9; UK 4.4 -> 0.7/1.7/2.5; all bilateral+EU 96.5 -> about 40/64/77. New multilateral (not yet in the map): IMF 0.9/3.1/5.2, World Bank 0.16/0.31/0.73, EBRD 0.06/0.36/1.0, CEB 0.04/0.12/0.22. Poland's USD 1bn swap line (0.88 in Kiel's financial aid) is worth ~0.01. The grant element is very sensitive to the discount rate for 35-year loans (MFA+ 2023: 0.54 at 7% with the subsidy ending 2027, 0.80 at 10% with it to 2034, 0.94 at 15% for the loan's life); see sensitivity table. Multilateral crediting by shareholding gives small amounts to countries that gave no bilateral aid (China 0.23, India 0.10, Brazil 0.08, Saudi Arabia 0.08 central; about 7% of capital in small members stays unassigned) - an artefact of the shareholding rule that the builder may prefer to show separately or omit for non-voting/opposing members.
